title: Data & AI Governance Leader, MD
description: Who We are looking for Data & AI Governance Leader, MD position is responsible to define and maintain enterprise Data, AI policies, standards, and governance operating model and serve a key point person for regulatory, audit, and supervisory engagement. The role operates proactively, anticipating regulatory direction and strengthening the firm’s posture ahead of examinations. It actively engages in all ongoing regulatory efforts related to data, risk, and AI, partnering with appropriate bank owners to ensure coordinated execution and durable remediation. In partnership with each line of business, this role defines the target state for Data and AI governance, ensuring clarity and consistency across ownership, stewardship, authoritative sourcing, data quality, and approval expectations. The role is intentionally independent of platform build, model development, and use‑case delivery. Success is measured by regulatory confidence, enterprise trust, data quality, and speed enabled through strong governance and streamlined processes. What you will be responsible for Enterprise Data, AI & Agentic AI Governance Define, maintain, and evolve enterprise-wide policies, standards, and control frameworks for: Data governance and data management Responsible AI and AI risk classification Ensure governance applies across the full lifecycle of data and AI assets, from design through retirement. Strategic Governance Target State (LOB Partnership) Partner with each line of business to define and maintain the target state for Data and AI governance aligned to enterprise standards and regulatory expectations. Translate enterprise governance principles into domain‑specific, actionable models. Provide governance leadership into Data & AI roadmaps without owning delivery or architecture decisions. Data Quality & Data Incident Management Define enterprise standards for data quality measurement, monitoring, and control. Own enterprise processes for data issues and incidents, including root cause analysis, remediation tracking, and escalation. Partner with business and platform teams to embed preventive and detective quality controls. Regulatory Leadership & Proactive Engagement Act as the lead for regulatory, audit, and supervisory engagement. Proactively assess emerging regulatory expectations and drive early alignment across the firm. Coordinate and participate in all active regulatory efforts relating to data, technology, and AI, working with appropriate bank owners. Lead regulatory examinations, findings, and remediation programs (e.g., BCBS 239, MRAs). Ensure regulatory learnings are converted into durable governance and process improvements. Education and Preferred Qualifications Required 12+ years of experience in Data Governance, Data Management, AI Governance, Technology Risk, Operational Risk, Regulatory Affairs, or related disciplines. Significant experience operating within highly regulated financial services organizations. Demonstrated experience working directly with regulators and supervisory bodies, including FRB, ECB, OCC, PRA, MAS, FCA, or equivalent agencies. Deep understanding of Data Governance, Data Quality, Data Risk Management, Data Lineage, Metadata Management, and AI Governance frameworks. Experience supporting regulatory examinations, audits, remediation programs, and enterprise risk initiatives. Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders across business and technology functions. Proven ability to lead complex cross-functional initiatives without direct authority. Preferred Experience with BCBS 239, enterprise data management regulations, model risk management, and Responsible AI frameworks. Familiarity with NIST AI RMF, emerging AI regulations, and global supervisory expectations for AI governance. Knowledge of governance platforms and technologies such as Collibra, Informatica, Microsoft Purview, Alation, or similar solutions. Advanced degree in Business, Technology, Data Management, Risk Management, or a related field. Salary Range: $170,000 - $282,500 Annual The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ. Employees are eligible to participate in State Street’s comprehensive benefits program, which includes: our retirement savings plan (401K) with company match; insurance coverage including basic life, medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, and other optional additional coverages; paid-time off including vacation, sick leave, short term disability, and family care responsibilities; access to our Employee Assistance Program; incentive compensation including eligibility for annual performance-based awards (excluding certain sales roles subject to sales incentive plans); and, eligibility for certain tax advantaged savings plans. title: Director, AI Risk, Return and Resilience
description: At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection. Job Description The Director, AI Risk, Return and Resilience will provide critical oversight, strategy and thought leadership over the governance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) at Allstate. This role is accountable for leading the enterprise AI risk, return and resilience strategy and programs, with a specific focus on the integration and management of AI, data, and model integration into the company as well as maintaining a robust governance structure. The role requires heavy coordination cross-functionally across areas of responsibilities and interaction with senior leadership. This role will be responsible for managing sub-teams devoted to assessment of AI internally and at third parties, and will work laterally with technologists, data scientists, modelers, legal and compliance personnel, other risk professionals, and business leaders. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Lead the enhancement and execution of a robust enterprise AI risk, return and resilience strategy that incorporates agentic and generative AI considerations Lead and coordinate the implementation of agentic, generative and broader AI deployment requirements across the enterprise Advance, automate and monitor progress over the various tracks of the AI risk program to drive efficiency and alignment with organizational goals and industry best practices. Provide thought leadership and oversight over the intake, enablement, and risk management of AI both internally and related to third parties Enhance, review and formalize policies and standards for AI risk management, specifically addressing the unique challenges and opportunities presented by AI technologies developed internally and externally Lead and oversee the intake and assessments over AI models, ensuring compliance with governance frameworks and ethical standards Lead and further embed AI model governance controls across 1st and 2nd line, including the proactive identification of AI models as they are deployed / modified Oversee the requirements over AI deployment platform implementations and articulate needs from an AI risk management perspective Contribute to support AI Working Group, Operational Risk and Return Council (ORRC), Enterprise Risk and Return Council (ERRC) and Board Risk and Return Committee (RRC) reporting SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES This job has supervisory duties. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 4 year Bachelors Degree (Preferred) 15 or more years of experience (Preferred) In lieu of the above education requirements, an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered. CERTIFICATIONS, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS No Certification, License or Registration is required for the job. title: AI GRC Architect
description: Calling all innovators - find your future at Fiserv. We're Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants and consumers to one another millions of times a day - quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we're involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv. Job Title AI GRC Architect About this role You will own the enterprise AI Governance architecture roadmap and technical implementation for OneTrust and associated GRC platforms, ensuring seamless integration, strong governance controls, and alignment with enterprise risk and compliance objectives. This role defines how Responsible AI policy is translated into scalable technical controls, lifecycle gates, and evidence models across business units. You will establish target-state architecture for AI intake, risk tiering, control mapping, approval workflows, continuous monitoring, and audit-ready traceability. Partnering with program owners, cyber/risk stakeholders, legal/compliance teams, and platform engineering, you will deliver governed designs that scale from pilot through production with clear operating ownership. What you’ll do: Define and lead enterprise architecture for AI Governance and Cyber GRC workflows, including standardized risk/control/evidence operating models. Own end-to-end AI governance lifecycle design: intake, classification, risk tiering, review/approval gates, exception handling, monitoring, and periodic reassessment. Translate policy and regulatory obligations into technical control patterns and reusable architecture blueprints deployable across UAT and production. Design and govern resilient API integrations across OneTrust, Archer, and broader enterprise systems, including SaaS-to-on-premise and hybrid environment constraints. Establish role, group, and organizational segmentation architecture to enforce least-privilege access and scalable governance operations. Lead architecture decisions for automation, error handling, observability, incident response, and production support readiness. Chair cross-functional architecture reviews and influence risk, compliance, and engineering decision forums on control design and prioritization. Mentor engineers and analysts through architecture standards, implementation playbooks, and design quality reviews. What success looks like in the first 12 months: AI governance workflows are standardized and operating consistently across major business domains. Manual evidence collection effort is materially reduced through automation and reusable control patterns. Assessment cycle times improve with clearer lifecycle gates, ownership, and exception pathways. Audit and regulatory traceability are strengthened with high-confidence control-to-evidence lineage. Deep integration engineering expertise: REST APIs, OAuth, reliability patterns, dependency governance, and production-grade operational resilience. Strong software and scripting capability (for example Python, JavaScript, and API-driven automation) with flexibility to work across unfamiliar stacks when needed. Experience translating business and regulatory requirements into control taxonomies, implementation plans, and governed technical workflows. Strong executive and technical communication skills, including architecture decision records, stakeholder alignment, and risk tradeoff articulation. Proven experience leveraging GRC platforms to operationalize compliance requirements across frameworks including SOC 2, HITRUST, NIST AI RMF, and PCI DSS through automated assessments, continuous control monitoring, evidence management, and compliance reporting. Experience that would be great to have: Strong OneTrust experience across multiple modules (for example IT Risk Management, Assessment Automation, Data Mapping, Privacy Rights, Consent, and related capabilities). Experience leading vendor/platform gap remediation, escalation strategies, and workaround playbooks in regulated enterprise environments. title: Sr. Analyst, AML Governance
description: About the Role We are hiring a Senior Analyst for AML Governance & Advisory within Financial Crimes & Identity. This team owns the governance framework supporting Chime's BSA/AML and OFAC compliance programs, ensuring that policies, procedures, controls, and reporting structures align with regulatory expectations, partner bank contractual obligations, internal risk appetite, and evolving financial crime risks. This position requires someone who thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and can balance regulatory rigor with operational agility. The ideal candidate is proactive, assertive, and solutions-oriented, capable of driving initiatives forward, challenging the status quo, and identifying opportunities to automate and streamline governance processes. The analyst partners cross-functionally with Compliance, Risk, Legal, Financial Crimes’ Operations, Product, and Engineering to drive effective oversight, documentation, and continuous program maturity. You will partner cross-functionally with Compliance, Risk, Legal, Financial Crimes Operations, Product, and Engineering to drive effective oversight, documentation, and continuous program maturity. The base salary offered for this role and level of experience will begin at $112,000.00 and up to $155,000.00. Full-time employees are also eligible for a bonus, competitive equity package, and benefits. The actual base salary offered may be higher, depending on your location, skills, qualifications, and experience.  In this role, you can expect to Lead and enhance governance frameworks supporting the BSA/AML and OFAC programs, ensuring clear ownership, accountability, and effective oversight. Drive governance routines, executive and committee reporting, and escalation processes in a fast-paced regulatory environment. Track, analyze, and report on program risks, issues, remediation plans, and control effectiveness to promote transparency and informed decision-making. Partner with Financial Crimes and Risk teams to support enterprise-wide AML and sanctions risk assessments, document controls and control owners, and strengthen the control framework. Draft, update, and maintain BSA/AML and OFAC policies, standards, and procedures in alignment with regulatory requirements and bank partner obligations. Monitor regulatory and guidance developments, assess applicability and impact to Chime, and drive the resulting policy and control updates to completion. Prepare comprehensive materials for regulatory exams, bank partner reviews, and internal/external audits, maintaining audit-ready documentation repositories. Coordinate audit and exam responses, and drive remediation efforts with clear milestones, measurable outcomes, and strong follow-through. Support issues management end to end — from issue intake and root cause analysis through corrective action plan design, validation, and sustainability evidence. Collaborate cross-functionally to influence outcomes, support change initiatives, and implement scalable governance improvements. To thrive in this role, you have 5+ years of experience in BSA/AML and OFAC compliance, with significant time spent in a governance, advisory, or second-line capacity at a fintech, bank, or other directly regulated financial institution. Deep working knowledge of FinCEN, OCC, and FFIEC requirements and examination expectations, with applied experience in consumer banking, payments, or lending. Exceptional written communication, with demonstrated ability to translate regulatory requirements into clear, defensible policies, procedures, and executive-level narratives. Experience supporting regulatory examinations, internal or external audits, and bank partner reviews — including request-list management, evidence collection, and interview preparation. Hands-on issues management experience: authoring corrective action plans, defining validation criteria, and tracking remediation to closure with evidence of sustainability. Experience contributing to enterprise-wide BSA/AML and sanctions risk assessments, including inherent risk scoring, control effectiveness rating, and residual risk methodology. Working knowledge of the three lines of defense model, and the judgment to provide credible independent challenge while maintaining strong first-line partnership. Experience building executive- or Board-level reporting materials and running formal governance and committee routines. A demonstrated record of driving automation or process improvement within a compliance or risk function. Strong program management skills, with the ability to run multiple concurrent workstreams against firm regulatory deadlines. Proven ability to influence across Compliance, Legal, Risk, Product, and Engineering. Comfort operating with urgency amid ambiguity, shifting priorities, and incomplete information.
